p1.original: 我们在前几章介绍了非暴力沟通的三个要素：观察、感受和需要。在本章中，我们将讨论非暴力沟通的第四个要素：请求。在表达观察、感受和需要之后，我们请求他人的帮助。以什么样的方式提出请求容易得到积极回应呢？
p1.en: In previous chapters, we have described three elements of Nonviolent Communication: observation, perception and need. In this chapter, we will discuss the fourth element of Nonviolent Communication: requests. After expressing our views, feelings and needs, we ask for the help of others. How can a request be easily responded to positively?

p3.original: 首先，清楚地告诉对方，我们希望他们做什么。如果我们请求他人不做什么，对方也许会感到困惑，不知道我们到底想要什么。而且，这样的请求还容易引起别人的反感。
p3.en: First, tell each other clearly what we want them to do. If we ask others not to do anything, the other side may be confused and wonder what we really want. Moreover, such a request can easily be offensive to others.

p4.original: 在一次研讨班中，一位女士谈道：“我请我先生少花一些时间在工作上。三个星期后，他和我说，他已经报名参加高尔夫球比赛。”这位女士说出了她不想要什么——她不希望先生花太多的时间在工作上，但没有说清楚她想要什么。于是，我们鼓励她直接说出愿望，她想了想，说道：“我希望他每周至少有一个晚上在家陪我和孩子。”
p4.en: In a workshop, a woman said, “I ask my husband to spend less time on his work. Three weeks later, he told me he had signed up for golf. “The woman said she did not want anything — she did not want him to spend too much time at work, but did not make it clear what she wanted. So we encouraged her to say what she wanted, and she thought, and she said, "I hope he'll be home with me and the kids at least one night a week.

p5.original: 在越战期间，我被邀请去参加电视辩论。晚上在家看节目的录像带时，我十分不安，因为我很不喜欢自己的辩论方式。我告诫自己：“在下一次辩论时，决不能再这么被动。”请注意，我只是提醒自己要避免出现什么，而没有提醒自己主动做些什么。
p5.en: During the Vietnam War, I was invited to participate in the television debate. I was very upset when I was watching the video at home at night, because I didn't like the way I debated. I caution myself: “The next debate must not be so passive again. “Please note that I am merely reminding myself of what to avoid, and not of what to do on my own initiative.

p6.original: 一周以后，这个节目邀请我去继续上一次的辩论。在去演播室的路上，我不断地提醒自己不要犯同样的错误。节目一开始，对手就按其上周的方式展开了辩论。他结束讲话后，大概有10秒，我努力控制自己不要按原来的方式进行回应。于是，我坐在那里，一句话也没说。可是，我一开始辩论，就发现我回应对手的方式和上次一模一样。这个教训使我明白了：如果我只是提醒自己要避免什么，而不清楚自己可以做什么，会有怎样的后果。
p6.en: A week later, I was invited to continue the last debate. On my way to the studio, I kept reminding myself not to make the same mistake. At the beginning of the programme, the rivals began their debate as they had done last week. I tried to control myself from responding in the way he did, about 10 seconds after he had finished. So I sat there, and I didn't say a word. However, at the outset of my debate, I found that I responded to my opponent in the same way as last time. That lesson made me understand what would happen if I merely reminded myself of what to avoid and wondered what to do.

p7.original: 另有一次，我应邀去协调一些高中生与他们校长的矛盾。这些高中生对校长极为不满。他们认为他是种族主义者，并准备找机会报复他。一位牧师担心会出现暴力，就请我去协调矛盾。出于对这位牧师的尊重，他们表示愿意与我见面。
p7.en: On another occasion, I was invited to coordinate some of the high school students' conflicts with their principals. These high school students are extremely dissatisfied with the principal. They consider him to be a racist and are prepared to seek an opportunity to retaliate against him. A priest who feared violence asked me to coordinate the conflict. Out of respect for the priest, they offered to meet with me.

p8.original: 一开始，他们就举例说明为什么他们认为校长是种族主义者。听完几个例子后，我请他们讲讲他们希望校长具体怎么做。
p8.en: At the outset, they gave examples of why they considered the headmaster to be racist. Having heard a few examples, I asked them to tell them what they wanted the headmaster to do.

p9.original: 此时，一位学生不屑地说：“这有什么用吗？每一次和他说我们的想法，他总是说‘离开这里！我不需要你们这些人告诉我该做什么！’”
p9.en: At this point, a student said with a displeasure: "What's the point? Every time he tells him what we think, he always says, "Get out of here! I don't need you people to tell me what to do! # # # # # # # I don't know #

p10.original: 接着，我向他们了解，他们向校长提出了什么请求。他们回忆说，他们希望校长不要对学生的长发说三道四。对此，我的看法是，如果他们说出希望校长做的事，而不是不希望他做的事，他们就较有可能得到积极的回应。此外，他们还提出，他们希望得到公平的对待。然而，校长的答复是，他对学生十分公平。我评论说，如果他们请求的是具体的行动，而非抽象的“公平对待”，那么，他们就较有可能得到满足。
p10.en: And then I knew what they were asking the headmaster. They recalled that they wanted the headmaster not to say anything about the students ' long hair. In response, my view is that if they say what they want the headmaster to do, not what they don't want, they are more likely to get a positive response. In addition, they stated that they wanted to be treated fairly. However, the headmaster responded that he was very fair to the students. I observed that if they were asking for concrete action, rather than an abstract “fair treatment”, they would be more likely to be satisfied.

p11.original: 于是，我和学生们一起列出了他们的具体请求，共有38项。其中包括：“我们希望黑人学生代表可以参加校服标准的制定。”“在你提到我们时，我们希望你用‘黑人学生’，而不是‘你们这些人’。”第二天，他们向校长提交了书面请求。当晚，他们就在电话中兴高采烈地告诉我，校长同意了所有的请求！
p11.en: So I joined the students in listing their specific requests, 38 of them. Among other things, “We would like to see black student representatives participate in the development of standards for school uniforms. “When you mention us, we want you to use `black students' instead of `you people'. The following day, they submitted a written request to the headmaster. That night, they told me on the phone that the headmaster had granted all requests!

p12.original: 我们提出的请求越具体越好。如果我们的意思含糊不清，别人就难以了解我们到底想要什么。有一幅卡通画描述的是一个人掉到了湖里。在湖中挣扎时，他冲着岸上的狗喊道：“快去求助！”在第二幅画中，这只狗躺在精神病医生的诊断台上。这个故事反映了人们对于“帮助”的含义可能存在不同的看法。
p12.en: The more specific our requests are, the better. If we are vague, it is difficult for others to understand exactly what we want. There's a cartoon depicting a man falling into the lake. As he struggled in the lake, he cried out to the dogs on the shore: "Go to help!" In the second picture, the dog was lying on the diagnostic table of the psychiatrist. This story reflects the different views that may exist about what “help” means.

p13.original: 此外，使用抽象的语言还会使我们无法深入了解自己。请求他人采取具体的行动将揭示我们的动机。一对夫妇在参加非暴力沟通研讨班时发生了争吵。太太对先生说：“我认为你应该让我成为我自己。”先生反驳：“我没有吗？”太太气冲冲地说：“你当然没有！”于是，先生就问太太她到底想要什么，太太回答说：“我希望你给我自由！”然而，这样的请求还是过于抽象，不具有可操作性。当她试图澄清她的请求时，她突然意识到了她想要什么。她说：“不好意思。准确地说，我希望，不论我做什么，你都能点头称是。”
p13.en: Moreover, the use of abstract language will prevent us from getting to know ourselves in depth. Requesting specific action from others will reveal our motives. A couple had an argument during a Nonviolent Communication workshop. The wife said to him, "I think you should make me myself. "Mr. Rebekah said, "I didn't? "Of course you didn't! So the gentleman asked his wife what she wanted, and she said, "I want you to set me free! However, such requests are too abstract and not operational. When she tried to clarify her request, she suddenly realized what she wanted. She said, "Sorry. To be precise, I hope that whatever I do, you can nod your head. I'm sorry.

p14.original: 有一次，我为一对父子提供心理咨询服务。在咨询的过程中，父亲对年仅15岁的孩子说：“我只是希望你能有一点责任感。这个要求难道过分吗？”这时，我请他说明，他的儿子怎样做才算是有责任感。于是，他就向我解释他对孩子的期待。最后，这位父亲说：“当我说我希望他能有点责任感时，我实际的意思是，他要听话，而不要固执己见。”他承认，即使他的孩子真的很听话，也不能说明他是否有责任感。
p14.en: I once provided psychological counselling to a couple of fathers and sons. During the consultation process, the father said to the 15-year-old child: “I just want you to have a sense of responsibility. Is that too much to ask? I asked him then to explain how his son was responsible. So he explained to me what he expected of him. Finally, the father said, “When I said I wanted him to have a sense of responsibility, what I actually meant was that he wanted to listen, not be stubborn. He admits that even if his child is really good, it does not show whether he has a sense of responsibility.

p15.original: 抽象的语言无助于深化自我认识。和这位父亲一样，在使用抽象的语言表达愿望时，我们一般不会提及我们可以做的事情。例如，为了了解企业的实际情况，公司经理对员工说：“我希望你们和我在一起时，不要有什么压力，什么话都可以说。”这句话反映了管理者希望员工“不要有什么压力”。如果管理者想让他的请求更具建设性，他可以说：“你们是否可以告诉我，我怎样做，你们在和我谈话时才能放得开？”
p15.en: Abstracted language does not help to deepen self-perception. Like the father, we do not generally mention what we can do when we express our wishes in abstract language. For example, in order to understand the real situation in the enterprise, the manager of the company said to the employee: “I hope that when you're with me, you don't have to be pressured to say anything. The sentence reflects the manager's desire for staff to “do not put any pressure on them”. If the manager wanted his request to be more constructive, he could say, “Can you tell me what I am doing before you can let go when you talk to me?

p16.original: 最后，我想再举例说明抽象的语言如何妨碍了自我认识及与人交流。当我从事临床心理医生这一职业时，有许多人由于情绪低落而向我求助。以下是我和一个来访者的对话：
p16.en: Finally, I would like to give another example of how abstract language impedes self-awareness and communication. When I was in the profession of clinical psychologist, many people turned to me for help because of the low mood. Here is a conversation between me and a visitor:

p18.original: 她：“我不知道我想要什么。”
p18.en: She said, "I don't know what I want.

p19.en: I said, "I guess you'll say that.

p21.original: 我：“我认为，我们感到沮丧是因为我们未能实现自己的愿望。可是，我们努力去实现梦想了吗？社会总是期待我们成为好男孩或好女孩、好父亲或好母亲。如果我们依照社会的期待去做，我们感到沮丧也就不是什么令人吃惊的事情了。沮丧是我们为了迎合社会而付出的代价。如果你要过得快乐些，我想请你想想，为了改善你的生活，你希望他人做些什么？”
p21.en: I said, “I think that we are frustrated because we have not been able to fulfil our aspirations. But have we tried to make it happen? Society always expects us to be good boys or good girls, good fathers or good mothers. If we do what society expects, it is not surprising that we are frustrated. Frustration is the price we pay to accommodate society. If you want to be happy, I want you to think about what you want others to do to improve your life.

p22.original: 她：“我只是希望有人关心我。这没有什么不合理，不是吗？”
p22.en: She said, "I just want someone to care about me. There's nothing unreasonable about that, isn't there?

p23.original: 我：“这是一个好的开始。现在我想请你谈谈其他人怎么做才是关心你。例如，我现在可以做些什么吗？”
p23.en: I said, "This is a good start. Now I would like to ask you to talk about what others do to care about you. For example, what can I do now?

p25.original: 我：“可是，我并不清楚你具体期待什么。我希望你告诉我，我或别的人怎么做，才是按你期待的方式来关心你？”
p25.en: I said, "But I don't know what you're looking for. I want you to tell me what I or someone else does to care for you the way you want?

p27.original: 我：“是的，说清楚我们的请求有时是很困难的。可是，让我们想想，如果我们都不清楚自己想要什么，那对别人来说，就更难了！”
p27.en: I said, “Yes, it is sometimes difficult to clarify our request. But let's think, if we don't know what we want, it's harder for others!

p28.original: 她：“我开始明白我希望别人怎么关心我，不过，我不太好意思说出来。”
p28.en: She said, "I'm beginning to understand how much I want people to care about me, but I'm not sure how to say it.

p29.original: 我：“是的，这经常是令人尴尬的。你愿意告诉我你期待我或别的人做什么吗？”
p29.en: I said, "Yes, it's often embarrassing. Would you tell me what you expect me or someone else to do?

p30.original: 她：“当我说需要别人的关心时，我实际想要的是，即使我还没有察觉到自己的需要，其他人就能考虑到我的需要。而且，我希望我总是能得到这样的照顾。”
p30.en: She said, “When I say I need someone else's attention, what I really want is that even if I don't know what I need, others can take my needs into account. And, I hope I always get that kind of care.

p31.original: 我：“谢谢。如果是这样，我相信你已经明白了你的愿望很难实现。”
p31.en: I said, "Thank you. If that is the case, I'm sure you understand that your wish is difficult to achieve.

p32.original: 许多来向我求助的人后来发现，他们感到沮丧或灰心，很大程度上是因为他们不清楚自己对他人究竟有什么样的期待。
p32.en: Many of those who came to me for help later found that they were frustrated or discouraged, largely because they did not know what they expected of others.

p33.en: Clear the purpose of the conversation.

p34.original: 有的时候，我们并不需要直接提出请求。比如说，在房间里看电视的孩子叫道：“妈，我口渴了。”在这种情况下，很明显，她是希望妈妈给她拿饮料。
p34.en: Sometimes we do not need to make a direct request. For example, the kid who watched TV in the room said, "Mom, I'm thirsty. In this case, it's obvious that she wants her mother to get her drinks.

p35.original: 然而，在另一些时候，我们也许只是说出我们的不快，却误以为别人知道我们想要什么。例如，一位太太和先生说：“我叫你带瓶酱油回来，可是你忘了。好烦啊！”也许，太太是希望先生马上出去买酱油。但她先生可能会以为她只是在指责他。如果我们只是表达自己的感受，别人可能就不清楚我们想要什么。
p35.en: At other times, however, we may be just saying our discomfort but mistakenly thinking that others know what we want. For example, a wife and a gentleman said, "I asked you to bring a bottle of soy sauce back, but you forgot. It's annoying! "Maybe the wife wants to go out and buy sauce immediately. But her husband might think she was just accusing him. If we just express our feelings, others may not know what we want.

p36.original: 更为常见的是，我们在说话时，并不知道自己想要什么。表面上，我们是在与人谈话，实际上，更像是自说自话。这时，我们的谈话对象可能就不知道如何回应，甚至会感到局促不安。
p36.en: More often, when we speak, we do not know what we want. On the face of it, we're talking to people, actually, more like talking to ourselves. At this point, our interlocutors may not know how to respond, and may even feel uneasy.

p37.original: 有一次，我乘火车去机场，坐在我正对面的是一对夫妇。对于赶飞机的人来说，慢速行驶的火车是十分烦人的。过了一会儿，对面的那位先生就气冲冲地对太太说，“我从没有见过开得这么慢的火车！”他太太看起来有点不知所措，什么话也没说。通常，大多数的人在没有得到期待的反馈时，会将所说的话重复一遍。这位先生也是如此。接着，他就高声喊道：“我从没有见过开得这么慢的火车！”
p37.en: One time, I took the train to the airport, sitting opposite me in a couple. For those driving the plane, the slow-moving train is very annoying. After a while, the gentleman across the street said to his wife, "I've never seen a train so slow! "His wife seemed a little confused and didn't say anything. Usually, most people repeat what they say when they do not get the feedback they expect. The same is true of this gentleman. Then he shouted, "I've never seen a train drive so slow!

p38.original: 太太看起来更加局促不安。她转过头去，和他说：“这趟列车行驶的速度是由程序控制的。”我不认为，她先生会对这样的回答感到满意。事实上，她先生更为恼怒，更大声地嚷道：“我从没有见过开得这么慢的火车！”这时，太太终于失去了耐心，厉声地说：“那你想我怎么样？下去推火车？”于是，两个人都处于痛苦中！
p38.en: The wife seems more disturbed. She turned around and said, “The speed of the train is controlled by the program. I don't think her husband would be satisfied with such a response. In fact, her husband was even more angry and more loud, saying, "I have never seen a train so slow! At this point, the wife finally lost her patience and said, "What do you want me to do?" Take the train down? So, both of them are in pain!

p39.original: 这位先生想听到什么呢？我相信他想要的是理解。如果他太太意识到这一点，她也许会说：“你希望火车开得快一点，是担心误机吗？”
p39.en: What does this gentleman want to hear? I believe what he wants is understanding. If his wife realized that, she might say, "Do you want the train to go faster, is it a mistake?

p40.original: 在之前的对话中，太太感到了先生的不安，但不清楚他想要什么。然而，如果一个人提出了明确的请求，却没有提及感受和需要，也有可能导致交流的困难。例如，如果父母问“为什么还不去理发呢”，孩子一般会把它看作是命令或指责。如果父母想避免误解，那么，他们可以先说出感受和需要：“你的头发这么长，我们担心这会影响你的视线，特别是在骑自行车的时候。去理发好吗？”
p40.en: During the previous dialogue, the wife had felt uneasy about him, but it was not clear what he wanted. However, if a person makes a clear request without mentioning feelings and needs, it may also lead to communication difficulties. For example, if parents ask “why not cut their hair”, the child would generally view it as an order or a charge. If parents want to avoid misunderstandings, they can first say what they feel and what they need: “Your hair is so long that we fear it will affect your eyes, especially when riding a bicycle. Would you like to cut your hair?

p41.original: 有些人也许会说，“我没有什么请求，只是随便聊聊。”然而，我相信，我们在和另一个人说话的时候，总是希望有所回应。也许，我们想要的只是他人的理解——就像那位乘火车去机场的先生，我们希望有人倾听并了解我们的处境。或者，我们期待的是如实的反馈——我们想了解他人的真实想法。当然，有时我们希望他人采取某种行动。对自己的认识越深刻，表达越清楚，我们就越可能得到称心的回应。
p41.en: Some people might say, "I don't have any requests, I just want to talk. However, I believe that when we speak to someone else, we always wish to respond. Perhaps all we want is the understanding of others — just like the gentleman on the train to the airport, we want someone to listen to and understand our situation. Or, what we are looking for is true feedback — we want to know the real thoughts of others. Sometimes, of course, we want others to do something. The deeper we know ourselves, the clearer we express ourselves, the more likely we will be to receive a well-deserved response.

p43.original: 我们的意思和别人的理解有时可能是两回事。如果无法确定对方是否已经明白，我们可能就需要得到反馈。请求反馈能确保对方准确把握我们的意思。有时，问一句“我的意思清楚吗”，然后，对方表个态就足够了。在另一些时候，听到“是的，我明白你的意思”这样的回答，我们并不放心。为了确保对方确实明白我们的意思，我们希望他充分表达他的理解。这样，一旦他的理解与我们的意思有所不同，我们就有机会作适当的补充。
p43.en: Our meaning and others' understanding may sometimes be different. If it is not possible to determine whether the other party has understood, we may need feedback. Requesting feedback ensures that the other party has an accurate understanding of what we mean. Sometimes, the question is, “Do I mean it clearly” and then the other side is enough. At other times, we are not reassured by the answer to “Yes, I understand what you mean”. In order to ensure that the other side really understands what we mean, we hope that he will fully express his understanding. In this way, once his understanding is different from what we mean, we have the opportunity to add it appropriately.

p44.original: 例如，一位老师和她的学生说：“托尼，今天批改作业时没有看到你的作业本。我想知道，你是否清楚我上次布置的作业。放学时，来我办公室一下好吗？”托尼咕噜了一句：“好，知道了。”然后，他就转过身去，准备离开了。老师站在那里，不清楚学生是否已经明白她的意思。于是，她叫住他：“麻烦你说一遍我刚才请你做的事情好吗？”托尼回答说：“放学后，我没法看足球赛了，因为你要把我留下来做作业。”老师发现托尼并没有听明白她的意思，她准备作出解释。这时，她很注意她的方式。
p44.en: For example, one teacher and her student said: “Tony, you didn't see your book at the time of the batch today. I was wondering if you knew about my last assignment. Can you come to my office after school? "Tony grunted, "Okay, got it. Then he turned around and was ready to leave. The teacher stood there and it was not clear whether the students understood what she meant. So she stopped him: "Can you tell me what I just asked you to do? Tony said, "After school, I can't watch football, because you're gonna leave me to do my homework. The teacher found out that Tony was not listening to her, and she was prepared to explain. And then she's paying attention to her way.

p45.original: 像“你没有听明白”“这不是我的意思”“你听错了”这样的表达，很可能会让托尼觉得老师在批评他。因为托尼很坦率地作出反馈，这位老师先向托尼表达了她的谢意。她说：“谢谢你给我反馈。我想我说得不够清楚。我的意思是，放学后，我给你讲讲我上次布置的作业。”
p45.en: An expression like "you don't understand," "that's not what I mean," "you're wrong," might make Tony think the teacher was criticizing him. The teacher first expressed her gratitude to Tony for his frank feedback. She said, "Thank you for giving me feedback. I don't think I'm clear enough. I mean, after school, I'll tell you about my last assignment.

p46.original: 第一次请求他人给我们这样的反馈时，我们也许会有点不自然。因为在生活中，我们很少提出这种请求。在强调这样做的重要性时，我常听到人们表达保留意见。他们担心，有的人也许会说“难道我是聋子？”或者“不要在我这里卖弄你的沟通技巧”。为了避免这种反应，我们可以先解释我们的目的——我们是为了了解我们是否已经把意思说清楚了。然而，如果对方说“我已经明白了，我没有那么蠢！”那么，我们可以体会他的感受和需要，并表达对他的尊重及我们的需要。
p46.en: We may be a little off-the-shelf when we first ask someone to give us such feedback. Because in life we rarely make such requests. In emphasizing the importance of doing so, I have often heard reservations expressed. They were worried that some people might say, "Are I deaf? Or, "Don't sell your communication skills to me." In order to avoid such a reaction, we can first explain our purpose — we are trying to see whether we have made our meaning clear. But if the other side says, "I understand, I'm not that stupid! So we can feel his feelings and needs and express our respect for him and our needs.

p48.original: 在确认对方已经明白后，我们常常会急于了解对方的反应。一般来说，我们关心的内容大致可以分为以下三方面：
p48.en: We are often anxious to understand each other's reactions when it is confirmed that the other party has understood them. Generally speaking, our concerns can be broadly divided into the following three areas:

p49.en: (a) How the other side feels at this moment

p50.original: 有时，我们想了解对方的感受，以及为什么他们会产生那样的感受。为此，我们也许会问：“听我说这些，你的心情怎么样？”然后，我们可以进一步问：“为什么呢？”
p50.en: Sometimes we want to know how the other side feels and why they feel that way. So, we might ask, "Listen to me, how are you feeling? Then we can ask, "Why?"

p52.original: 有时，我们想了解对方的想法。在询问时，说清楚想了解的是哪方面的想法，将有助于我们获得所需的回应。例如，我们可以和对方说：“我想请你谈谈我的建议是否有可行性。如果不太可行，那根据你的判断，哪些因素会妨碍建议的实施呢？”如果我们只是问“对这个建议你有什么看法”，那么，对方谈的内容也许并不是我们关心的。
p52.en: Sometimes we want to know each other's thoughts. When asked, to say clearly which aspects of the idea are in question would help us to obtain the required response. For example, we can say to each other: “I would like to ask you to comment on the feasibility of my proposal. If not, what factors, in your judgement, would impede the implementation of the recommendations? “If we are just asking “what do you think of this proposal”, then perhaps the content of the other party's talk is not our concern.

p53.en: (c) Whether the other party accepts our request

p54.original: 在另一些时候，我们可能想知道，对方是否愿意接受我们的请求。这时，我们也许会问：“我想知道，你是否同意将会议时间推迟一周？”
p54.en: At other times, we may wonder whether the other side is willing to accept our request. At this point, we might ask: “I wonder, do you agree to postpone the meeting by one week?

p55.original: 在了解对方的反应时，我们要能意识到我们想了解的是哪方面的内容，并提出明确的请求。
p55.en: In understanding each other's reactions, we need to be aware of what we want to know and to make clear requests.

p56.original: 在集体讨论时提出请求
p56.en: Request made during the collective discussion

p57.original: 参加集体讨论时，说清楚我们希望得到怎样的反馈，是至关重要的。如果不清楚发言的目的，我们的讨论也许只是在浪费时间，而无法满足任何人的需要。
p57.en: It is essential to make clear in the collective discussions what feedback we would like to receive. If the purpose of the statement is not clear, our discussion may be a waste of time and not a meeting of the needs of anyone.

p58.original: 有一些关心种族歧视问题的团体曾邀请我去协助他们的工作。其中一个原因是他们的会议常常既沉闷又没有成效。而为了参加这些会议，参加者不仅要托人照顾孩子，而且还要将有限的资金用来支付交通费用。于是，许多人退出了这些团体。他们认为参加这些团体的会议毫无意义。此外，实现这些团体所寻求的机构变革需要长期的努力。因此，使会议变得富有成效对他们来说是十分重要的。
p58.en: Some groups concerned with racial discrimination have invited me to assist them in their work. One reason for this is that their meetings are often both boring and ineffective. In order to participate in these meetings, participants must not only place children in care, but also devote limited funds to cover transportation costs. As a result, many people withdrew from these groups. They saw no point in participating in the meetings of these groups. Moreover, achieving the institutional changes sought by these groups requires a long-term effort. It was therefore important for them to make the Conference a productive one.

p59.original: 有一个团体成立的目的是为了推动当地学校的改革。他们认为这些学校没有公平地对待各个种族的学生。为了提高会议效率和避免成员的进一步减少，这个团体请我去旁听他们的会议。于是，我应邀参加了会议。
p59.en: One group was formed to promote reform of local schools. They believe that these schools do not treat students of all races fairly. In order to improve the efficiency of meetings and avoid further reductions in membership, the group asked me to attend their meetings. So I was invited to the meeting.

p60.original: 会议一开始，一位先生就讲到最近报纸发表的一篇文章。这篇文章的作者是一位少数族裔的妇女。她在文章中抱怨她的女儿在学校中受到校方不公正的对待。接着，有一位女士介绍她自己在这所学校中的个人经历。紧接着，其他人也开始讲类似的经历。20分钟后，我问与会人员，目前的讨论是否能够满足他们的需要。没有一个人说“可以”。其中一位先生有点气恼地说：“这些会议总是这样！做别的事比在这里听废话好得多！”
p60.en: At the beginning of the meeting, a gentleman spoke about an article published in a recent newspaper. The author of this article is a woman from an ethnic minority. In her article, she complained that her daughter had been unfairly treated by the school. A woman then presented her personal experience at the school. Next, others began to share similar experiences. Twenty minutes later, I asked the participants whether the current discussions would meet their needs. No one says “yes”. One of the gentlemen was a little upset to say, “These meetings are always like this!” It's better to do something else than to listen to crap here!

p61.original: 于是，我就问开始这个话题的那位先生：“你提到那篇文章，是想得到怎样的反馈呢？”他回答说：“我认为这篇文章很有意思。”我解释说，我想知道的是他期待得到怎样的反馈，而不是他对这篇文章的看法。他想了想，然后承认：“我不知道我想要什么。”
p61.en: So I asked the gentleman who started the topic: "What kind of feedback did you want to get when you mentioned the article? He replied, "I think this article is interesting. I explained that what I wanted to know was what kind of feedback he expected, not what he thought of the article. He thought about it, and he said, "I don't know what I want.

p62.original: 我想，这就是会议的前20分钟讨论毫无成效的原因。如果我们在集体讨论时漫无目的地发言，那么，会议很可能就会毫无成果。然而，只要有一个人能够意识到这一点，他就可以提醒会议的其他成员有针对性地展开讨论。例如，在那位先生没有讲清他提及那篇文章的目的时，其他成员就可以和他说：“我不清楚你为什么要提到这篇文章。你是否可以告诉我们，你期待得到怎样的反馈呢？”这样的提醒也许就可以避免浪费宝贵的会议时间。
p62.en: That, I think, is why the discussions in the first 20 minutes of the meeting were fruitless. If we take the floor in collective discussions without purpose, then the Conference is likely to be fruitless. However, as long as one person was aware of that, he could alert the other members of the Conference to a focused discussion. For example, when the same man did not explain the purpose of his reference to the article, other members could say to him: “I do not know why you mentioned it. Can you tell us what kind of feedback you expect? Such a reminder might avoid wasting valuable meeting time.

p63.original: 此外，如果不清楚发言者是否已经得到满意的答复，讨论就可能漫无目的地继续下去，而无法满足任何人的需要。在印度，如果发言者得到了他所需要的回复，他就会说“bas”（这个词发音同“巴士”）。这意味着：“谢谢你！我已经明白了。”虽然，我们的语言中没有这样一个词，但我们可以在交流中具备这种意识。
p63.en: Moreover, if it was not clear whether the speaker had received a satisfactory response, the discussion might continue without purpose and without meeting the needs of anyone. In India, if the speaker had the answers he needed, he would have said “bas”. It means, "Thank you! I understand. While there is no such word in our language, we can have that sense in communication.

p65.original: 一旦人们认为不答应我们就会受到责罚，他们就会把我们的请求看作是命令。听到命令时，一个人只能看到两种选择：服从或反抗。不论如何，只要人们认为我们是在强迫他们，他们就不会乐于满足我们的需要。如果我们在过去常常指责他人，那么，我们的请求很可能就会被看作是命令。而一个经常受到指责的人也会倾向于将请求解读为命令。
p65.en: Once people feel that we will be punished for failing to do so, they will regard our request as an order. When an order is given, one can only see two options: obedience or resistance. In any case, as long as people think we are forcing them, they will not be happy to meet our needs. If we have often accused others in the past, then our request is likely to be seen as an order. A frequently accused person would also tend to interpret a request as an order.

p66.original: 以下我们用一个例子来说明请求与命令的区别。
p66.en: We will give an example of the difference between a request and an order.

p67.original: 如何区分命令和请求：请求没有得到满足时，提出请求的人如果批评和指责，那就是命令；如果想利用对方的内疚来达到目的，也是命令。
p67.en: (a) How to distinguish between orders and requests: where a request is not fulfilled, the person making the request is the order if he or she criticizes and accuses; It is also an order if you want to use the guilt of the other party to achieve its purpose.

p68.original: 杰克和他的朋友珍妮说：“我很孤单，希望今晚你能陪我聊聊。”这是请求还是命令呢？现在还不好说。我们需要根据珍妮没有同意时杰克的反应来作出判断。假定她回答说：“杰克，我今天很累。如果你想今晚有人陪你，你去找其他人好不好？”如果杰克接着说：“你这人真自私！”那么，他的提议实际上就是命令。因为他并没有重视珍妮休息的需要，而开始指责她。
p68.en: Jack and his friend Jenny said, "I'm lonely and I hope you can talk to me tonight. Is this a request or an order? It's hard to say now. We need to judge on the reaction of Jack when Jenny does not agree. Suppose she answered, "Jack, I'm tired today. If you want someone to stay with you tonight, why don't you go find someone else? If Jack goes on and says, "You're so selfish! So his proposal is actually an order. Because he didn't care about Jenny's need for rest, he started blaming her.

p69.original: 以下是对话以另一种方式展开：
p69.en: The following dialogue took place in another way:

p70.original: 杰克：“我很孤单，希望今晚你能陪我聊聊。”
p70.en: Jack: "I'm lonely and I hope you can talk to me tonight.

p71.original: 珍妮：“杰克，我真的很累。如果你想今晚有人陪你，找别人好不好？”
p71.en: "Jake, I'm really tired. If you want someone to stay with you tonight, why don't you find someone else?

p73.original: 珍妮发现杰克不太高兴，就问他：“你怎么了？”
p73.en: Jenny found out Jack wasn't happy, and asked him, "What's wrong with you?

p75.original: 珍妮：“我觉得你好像有心事。来，说说看。”
p75.en: "Jeann: I think you have something on your mind. Come on, tell me.

p76.original: 杰克：“你知道我孤单极了。你要是真的爱我，今晚就会留下来陪我。”
p76.en: Jack: "You know I'm lonely. If you really love me, you'll stay with me tonight.

p77.original: 在这段对话中，杰克仍然没有重视珍妮的需要，而是认为珍妮不再爱他。我们越是将他人的不顺从看作是对我们的排斥，我们所表达的愿望就越有可能被看作是命令。这将导致恶性循环，因为一旦人们认为我们是在强迫他们，他们就会不太想满足我们的愿望。
p77.en: In this dialogue, Jack still did not take Jenny's needs seriously, but thought that Jenny no longer loved him. The more we perceive the insubordination of others as an exclusion from us, the more likely our expressed aspirations are to be seen as orders. This will lead to a vicious circle, because once people are seen to be forcing them, they will be less interested in meeting our aspirations.

p78.original: 反之，如果杰克尊重珍妮的感受和需要，那么他所表达的愿望就是请求而非命令。这时，杰克也许会说：“珍妮，你的意思是说，你已经很累了，今晚需要休息？”
p78.en: On the contrary, if Jack respects Jenny's feelings and needs, then his expressed wish is a request, not an order. And then Jack might say, "Jeann, you mean, you're tired and you need to rest tonight?

p79.original: 在生活中，如果我们不想勉强人，那么，清楚地表明这一点是重要的——这有助于人们相信我们提出的是请求而非命令。例如，我们可以说：“帮我打开窗户好吗？”而不是说：“请打开窗户！”然而，在人们无法满足我们的愿望时，我们是否尊重他们的感受和需要最能体现我们提出的是请求还是命令。如果我们愿意去体会是什么使他们无法说“是”，那么，根据我的定义，我们提出的就是请求而非命令。选择通过请求而非命令来表达愿望，并不意味着，一旦人们说“不”，我们就不再去满足自己的需要。但它意味着，除非已经充分体会是什么妨碍了他人说“是”，我们就不会试图说服他们。
p79.en: In life, if we do not want to be reluctant, then it is important to make this clear — to help people believe that we are making a request, not an order. For example, we could say, "Can you open the window for me? "Open the window, please! However, when people are unable to meet our aspirations, whether we respect their feelings and needs is the most reflective of whether we are asking or ordering. If we are willing to see what prevents them from saying “yes”, then, by my definition, we are asking, not ordering. The choice to express a wish through a request rather than an order does not mean that once people say “no”, we will no longer meet our needs. But it means that we will not try to convince others unless we have fully understood what prevents them from saying “yes”.

p81.original: 如果我们只是想改变别人，以使他们的行动符合我们的利益，那么非暴力沟通并不是适当的工具。非暴力沟通是用来帮助我们在诚实和倾听的基础上与人联系。使用非暴力沟通时，我们希望人们的改变和行动是出于对生命的爱。一旦人们相信我们看重彼此的感情，并能兼顾双方的需要，那么，他们也就会相信我们所表达的愿望是请求而非命令。
p81.en: Nonviolent Communication is not an appropriate tool if we simply want to change others in order to make their actions work in our interests. Nonviolent Communication is used to help us reach people on the basis of honesty and listening. In using Nonviolent Communication, we want people to change and act out of love for life. Once people believe that we value each other's feelings and that we can balance their needs, they will also believe that our expressed desire is a request rather than an order.

p82.original: 然而，坚持以非暴力沟通的方式与人沟通是很不容易的。对于父母、老师、经理以及其他处于管理位置的人来说，尤其如此。在一次研讨班中，有位母亲和我说：“马歇尔，我回家试过了，但没什么用。”于是，我请她讲讲发生了什么事情。
p82.en: It is, however, difficult to maintain Nonviolent Communication. This is particularly true for parents, teachers, managers and others in managerial positions. In a seminar, a mother said to me, "Marshall, I tried to go home, but it didn't work. So I asked her to tell me what happened.

p83.original: “回家后，就像上午练习时那样，我表达了感受和需要。我并没有责备孩子。我只是说‘当我看到你没有做你答应做的家务活，我十分失望。因为我希望回家后有个干净整洁的环境’。然后，我提出了请求：我请他立即把房间收拾干净。”
p83.en: “When I came home, I had felt and needed, as I did in the morning exercise. I didn't blame the kids. I'm just saying, "I'm very disappointed when I see you not doing the housework you promised. 'Cause I want a clean and clean environment when I get home'. Then I asked him to clean up the room immediately.

p84.original: “听起来你已经很清楚地表达了非暴力沟通的四个要素，”我回答说，“然后呢？”
p84.en: “You have clearly expressed the four elements of Nonviolent Communication,” I replied, “What then?

p86.en: "What about next? I'm going to ask.

p87.original: “我和他说，像他这样懒惰和不负责任的人是不会有什么前途的。”
p87.en: “I said to him that there is no future for a lazy and irresponsible person like him.

p88.original: 我注意到这位女士把请求和命令混为一谈。在她看来，非暴力沟通是否有用取决于她的“请求”是否能得到满足。在刚开始运用非暴力沟通时，我们也许会发现，有时我们只是在运用非暴力沟通的表达形式，而忘记了它所服务的目的。
p88.en: I note that the lady has confused the request with the order. In her view, the usefulness of Nonviolent Communication depended on the satisfaction of her “requests”. When we begin to use Nonviolent Communication, we may find that sometimes we are simply using non-violent forms of communication and forgetting what it serves.

p89.original: 然而，在另一些时候，即使我们以适当的方式提出请求，有些人仍会误以为是命令。特别是当我们处于强势的一方，那些曾受过权威威胁的人尤其容易作出那样的判断。
p89.en: At other times, however, even if we make a request in the proper manner, some may still misconstrue it as an order. Especially when we are on the strong side, those who have been threatened with authority are particularly easy to judge in that way.

p90.original: 有一次，一所高中的管理团队请我去示范如何运用非暴力沟通与学生沟通。我要会见的学生有四十位。在学校中，他们被看作是“品行不端”的学生。我认为，像“品行不端”这样的标签会带来很消极的影响。如果一个学生被贴上这样的标签，那岂不是说他不遵守学校规矩是正常的吗？这样的标签将鼓励学生做我们不希望他们做的事，然后，他们的行为似乎又进一步证实了我们的判断。
p90.en: On one occasion, a management team from a high school asked me to demonstrate how to use Nonviolent Communication to communicate with students. I have 40 students to meet. In schools, they are considered to be students of “disgraceful conduct”. I think labels such as "bad behavior" have a very negative impact. If a student is labeled like this, isn't it normal to say that he does not comply with the school rules? Such labels will encourage students to do what we do not want them to do, and then their behaviour seems to further confirm our judgment.

p91.original: 当我走进教室时，大部分的学生挤在窗口和楼下的同学互相叫骂。对此，我并不意外。一开始，我就提出请求：“请各位同学回座位坐好，我将做自我介绍，并谈谈来这里的目的。”大概有一半的学生回到了座位。为了让其他学生听清我的请求，我重复了一遍。这时，除了两位学生仍站在窗口，其他学生都在位子上坐了下来。他们是班上个子最大的两位学生。
p91.en: When I walked into the classroom, most of the students were crowded in windows and downstairs, yelling at each other. I'm not surprised about that. At the outset, I asked: “Please return to your seats and I will introduce myself and talk about the purpose of coming here. "About half of the students returned to their seats. To make my request clear to the other students, I repeat. At that time, all but two of the students were sitting on the window. They're the two biggest students in the class.

p92.original: “你们好，”我对他们说，“你们中哪一位愿意告诉我，我刚才说了什么？”其中一位学生转过来，粗声粗气地说：“你要求我们马上回到座位坐下来。”这让我明白了，他把我的请求当作了命令。
p92.en: "Hello," I said to them, "Who among you would like to tell me what I just said? One of the students turned around and said, "You asked us to go back to our seats and sit down right away." That makes me understand that he took my request as an order.

p93.original: 我接着问他：“你是否愿意告诉我，我怎样表达我的请求，你才不会认为我在发号施令？”“什么？”对于我这个问题，他很意外。于是，我解释说：“我的意思是，我怎样表达我的请求，你才会认为我也在乎你的需要呢？”他想了想，然后耸了耸肩，说道：“我不知道。”
p93.en: I went on to ask him, “Will you tell me how I'm going to express my request so you don't think I'm giving orders? "What? He's surprised about my problem. So I said, "I mean, how do I express my request so you think I care about your needs? He thought about it, and he shrugged his shoulder, and he said, "I don't know.

p94.original: “刚才的对话已经提到了我今天想讨论的话题。我认为，表达愿望时，只要不发号施令，我们的相处就会愉快得多。我说出我的愿望，并不是要求你照我说的去做。我不知道，怎么说，你才能相信这一点。”那位学生似乎明白了我的意思，听完我的话，他就和他的同学慢悠悠地走回了座位。可见，在一些情形中，对方也许需要一些时间来了解我们提出的是请求而非命令。
p94.en: “The dialogue that has just taken place has already referred to the topic that I would like to discuss today. I believe that we will be much happier when we express our wishes without giving orders. I do not ask you to do what I say. I don't know, how can you believe that. The student seemed to understand what I was saying, and after listening to me, he walked back to his fellow students. It is clear that in some cases the other party may need some time to understand that we are making a request rather than an order.

p95.original: 在提出请求前，如果我们有以下的想法，那么，我们的请求已经成为了对他人的要求。
p95.en: Before making a request, if we have the following ideas, then our request has become a demand on others.

p96.en: He should clean up the room.

p97.en: • She must do as I say.

p98.en: The boss should give me a raise.

p99.en: • I have the right to request a longer vacation.

p100.original: 如果我们有这样的想法，一旦别人没有满足我们的要求，我们难免就会指责他们。有一段时间，当我的小儿子布拉特没有倒垃圾时，我就有类似的想法。我们对家务活进行了分工，他负责倒垃圾。可是，他很不主动。为了让他去倒垃圾，每天我都会提醒他“这是你的任务”或“我们每个人都有自己的任务”。
p100.en: If we have such an idea, we will inevitably accuse others of failing to meet our demands. For a while, when my little son Blart didn't take out the trash, I had a similar idea. We have a division of household work, and he is responsible for the garbage disposal. But he's very reluctant. In order for him to take out the garbage, every day I remind him that “it is your task” or “each of us has his own task”.

p101.original: 后来，有一天晚上，我终于静下心来听他讲为什么他不愿倒垃圾。谈话后，我以《布拉特的心声》为题写下了一段话：
p101.en: Later, one night, I finally came to hear from him why he didn't want to take out the garbage. After the conversation, I wrote a message under the title " The Voice of Blart ":

p102.original: “在印象中，如果我没照你说的去做，你就不会尊重我。如果我知道你并不想使唤我，在你叫我时，我会乐于回应你。如果你高高在上，像个盛气凌人的老板，你将会发现，你一头撞在了墙上。当你反复提醒我，你为我做的各种事情，你最好准备再次碰壁！你可以大声抱怨、责骂，但我仍不会去倒垃圾。即使你现在改变方式，我也需要时间忘记不快。”
p102.en: “It seems to me that if I hadn't done what you said, you wouldn't have respected me. If I knew you didn't want to call me, I'd be happy to answer when you called me. If you're up high, like a boss, you'll find you hit a wall. When you keep reminding me that you've done everything for me, you better be ready to hit the wall again! You can complain out loud and scold, but I'm not going to take out the garbage. Even if you change the way you do it now, I need time to forget about it.

p103.original: 通过这次谈话，布拉特认为我已经理解并尊重他的立场。在以后的日子里，他每天都主动倒垃圾。
p103.en: Through this conversation, Blatter believes that I have understood and respected his position. In the days ahead, he takes out the garbage every day.

p105.original: 非暴力沟通的第四个要素是请求。我们告诉人们，为了改善生活，我们希望他们做什么。我们避免使用抽象的语言，而借助具体的描述，来提出请求。
p105.en: The fourth element of Nonviolent Communication is a request. We tell people what we want them to do to improve their lives. We avoid using abstract language, but instead use specific descriptions to make a request.

p106.original: 在发言时，我们将自己想要的回应讲得越清楚，就越有可能得到理想的回应。由于我们所要表达的意思与别人的理解有可能不一致，有时，我们需要请求他人的反馈。特别是在集体讨论中发言时，我们需要清楚地表明自己的期待。否则，讨论可能只是在浪费大家的时间。
p106.en: The clearer we speak for ourselves, the more likely it will be to get the desired response. Since the meaning we are about to express may not be consistent with the understanding of others, sometimes we need to ask for feedback from others. In particular, when speaking in collective discussions, we need to make our expectations clear. Otherwise, the discussion might be just a waste of time for all of us.

p107.original: 一旦人们认为不答应我们就会受到责罚，他们就会把我们的请求看作是命令。如果我们清楚地表达我们无意强人所难，人们一般会相信，我们提出的是请求而非命令。非暴力沟通的目的不是为了改变他人来迎合我们。相反，非暴力沟通重视每个人的需要，它的目的是帮助我们在诚实和倾听的基础上与人联系。
p107.en: Once people feel that we will be punished for failing to do so, they will regard our request as an order. If we make it clear that we have no intention of being strong, it is generally believed that we are making a request, not an order. Nonviolent Communication is not intended to change others to suit us. On the contrary, Nonviolent Communication takes into account the needs of everyone, and its purpose is to help us reach out to people on the basis of honesty and listening.

p109.en: Tell your best friends to quit smoking.

p110.original: 艾伦和卡特是有30多年交情的老朋友。卡特每天要抽两包烟。多年来，艾伦想尽一切办法来让卡特戒烟，但都没有成功。在过去的几年，卡特咳嗽得越来越厉害。有一天，艾伦终于忍不住和卡特再一次谈到了戒烟。
p110.en: Alan and Carter have been friends for over 30 years. Carter smokes two packs a day. For years, Alan tried everything to get Carter to quit smoking, but it didn't work. Carter's coughing up in the last few years. One day, Alan finally talked to Carter again about quitting smoking.

p112.original: 艾伦：“卡特，这个问题我们已经说过无数次了。不过，我还是想告诉你，我很害怕，你这样抽下去，很快就会完蛋！你是我最好的朋友，我不想失去你。请不要认为，我又在指责你。我真的没有。我只是很担心。”（在过去，艾伦在劝卡特戒烟时，常常会指责他。）
p112.en: Alan: Carter, we've talked about this a million times. But I want to tell you, I'm scared. You're gonna smoke it. It'll be over soon! You're my best friend. I don't want to lose you. Please don't think I'm accusing you again. I really didn't. I'm just worried. ”Alan often accused Carter of turning him off in the past. I don't think so.

p113.original: 卡特：“我知道你是在关心我。我们已经是老朋友了……”
p113.en: Carter: "I know you're concerned about me. We're old friends now."

p114.original: 艾伦：（提出请求）“你愿意戒烟吗？”

p115.en: Carter: "I wish I could do it.

p116.original: 艾伦：（了解卡特无法做到的原因）“你不想戒烟，是因为你担心自己做不到吗？”
p116.en: Alan: "You don't want to quit because you're afraid you can't do it?

p117.original: 卡特：“是的。你知道我已经戒过很多次了，但都没有成功。我想，别人会觉得我很没用。”
p117.en: Carter: Yes. You know I quit many times, but it didn't work out. I guess people would think I was useless.

p118.original: 艾伦：（猜测卡特会有什么请求）“我没有看轻你。即使你再次戒烟失败，我也不会看不起你。我只是希望你再试一试。”
p118.en: Alan: "I didn't take you lightly. Even if you fail again, I won't look down on you. I just want you to try again.

p119.original: 卡特：“谢谢。但又不是只有你一个人……从他们的眼中，我可以看出，他们认为我是个没用的人。”
p119.en: Carter: "Thank you. But you're not the only one... in their eyes, I can see that they think I'm a useless person.

p120.original: 艾伦：（体会卡特的感受和需要）“如果不是担心别人的看法，你就会愿意再次戒烟，是吗？”
p120.en: Alan: "If you weren't worried about what Carter felt and needed, you'd be willing to quit again, wouldn't you?

p121.original: 卡特：“我不喜欢自己有烟瘾。我不希望自己听任烟瘾的摆布……”
p121.en: Carter: "I don't like my addiction to tobacco. I don't want to let myself be at the mercy of the tobacco addiction..."

p122.original: 艾伦：（艾伦看着卡特的眼睛，点了点头。艾伦的眼神流露出他对卡特的关心。）
p122.en: Alan: Alan looked Carter in the eye, noded his head. Alan's eyes reveal his concern for Carter. I don't think so.

p123.original: 卡特：“我的意思是说，我已经不喜欢抽烟了。特别是在公共场合抽烟，我会觉得很不好意思。”
p123.en: Carter: I mean, I don't like smoking anymore. I'd be embarrassed to smoke in public. I'm sorry.

p124.original: 艾伦：（继续体会卡特的感受和需要）“听起来，你很想戒烟，可又担心会失败——你害怕这会影响到你的形象和信心。”
p124.en: Alan: "You sound like you want to quit smoking, but you're afraid of failure -- you're afraid that it will affect your image and your confidence.

p125.original: 卡特：“是的。我想这就是我的意思……你知道，我以前并没有提到这一点。当人们劝我戒烟时，我就会叫他们走开。我是想戒烟，但我不想任何人给我压力。”
p125.en: Carter: Yes. I guess that's what I mean... You know, I didn't mention that before. And when people persuade me to quit smoking, I will ask them to go away. I wanted to quit smoking, but I didn't want anyone to put pressure on me.

p126.original: 艾伦：“我不希望你有包袱。我也不知道能否打消你的顾虑，但我会尽力帮助你——只要你愿意。”
p126.en: Alan: I don't want you to be burdened. I don't know if I can help you out, but I'll do my best to help you if you want.

p127.original: 卡特：“我真的很感激你的关心。但是，如果我现在还做不到，你会介意吗？”
p127.en: Carter: I really appreciate your concern. But if I can't do it now, would you mind?

p128.original: 艾伦：“当然不会！我只是希望你的健康状况能变好。”（因为艾伦提出的是真诚的请求，而非要求，不论卡特有怎样的反应，他们的关系都不会受影响。）
p128.en: Alan: Of course not! I just want your health to be better. “Because Alan's request was sincere, not a request, and no matter how far Carter reacted, their relationship would be affected. I don't think so.

p129.original: 卡特：“谢谢！也许我会再试一次。但请你先不要告诉别人，好吗？”
p129.en: Carter: "Thank you! Maybe I'll try again. But please don't tell anyone, okay?

p130.original: 艾伦：“好的。你放心。我不会和任何人说的。”
p130.en: Allan: Okay. Don't worry. I won't talk to anyone.

p132.original: 根据你的观点，下列哪些句子提出了明确的请求？
p132.en: From your point of view, which of the following sentences makes a clear request?

p134.original: 2.请告诉我，在我做的事情中，你最满意的是哪一件？
p134.en: 2. Please tell me which of the things I have done you are most satisfied with.

p135.en: I want you to be more confident.

p138.original: 6.关于昨天的会议，请不要隐瞒你的看法。
p138.en: 6. With regard to yesterday's meeting, please do not hide your views.

p139.original: 7.我希望你能在规定的时速内驾驶。
p139.en: I hope you will drive at the required speed.

p140.en: I want to know you better.

p141.original: 9.我希望你尊重我的个人隐私。
p141.en: 9. I hope you respect my privacy.

p142.en: I hope you'll cook dinner often.

p143.original: 以下是我对练习4的理解：
p143.en: Here's my understanding of practice four:

p144.original: 1.如果你选择这一句，我们意见不一致。对我来说，在这个句子中，“理解”这个词并没有清楚地表达发言者的请求。如果发言者说“你是否可以告诉我，你认为我刚才说的是什么意思”，那么，我认为发言者提出了明确的请求。
p144.en: If you choose this sentence, we are not in agreement. For me, in this sentence, the word “understanding” does not clearly express the request of the speaker. If the speaker says, “Can you tell me what you think I just said”, then I think he made a clear request.

p145.original: 2.如果你选择这一句，我们意见一致。
p145.en: 2. If you choose this sentence, we agree.

p146.original: 3.如果你选择这一句，我们意见不一致。如果发言者说“我希望你能参加关于人际交流的培训，我相信这会有助于你增强自信心”，那么，我认为发言者提出了明确的请求。
p146.en: 3. If you choose this sentence, we are not in agreement. If the speaker says, “I hope that you will participate in training on interpersonal communication, which I believe will help you to be more self-confident”, then I think he has made a clear request.

p147.original: 4.如果你选择这一句，我们意见不一致。对我来说，这句话表达的是发言者想要避免的事情。如果发言者说“你是否可以告诉我，喝酒可以满足你什么需要？是否有别的方式可以满足那些需要”，那么，我认为发言者提出了明确的请求。
p147.en: 4. If you choose this sentence, we are not in agreement. For me, this sentence is an expression of what the speakers want to avoid. If the speaker said, “Can you tell me what you need to drink? There are other ways to meet those needs”, and I think the speaker made a clear request.

p148.original: 5.如果你选择这一句，我们意见不一致。对我来说，“让我成为我自己”是一个模糊的请求。如果发言者说“我希望你告诉我，即使你不喜欢我做的一些事情，你仍然会和我在一起”，那么，我认为发言者提出了明确的请求。
p148.en: 5. If you choose this sentence, we are not in agreement. To me, "Let me be myself" is a vague request. If the speaker says, “I want you to tell me that you will be with me even if you do not like what I do”, then I think he has made a clear request.

p149.original: 6.如果你选择这一句，我们意见不一致。对我来说，“不要隐瞒”是一个模糊的请求。如果发言者说“请告诉我，你怎么看我昨天在会议中的表现，给我一些建议好吗”，那么，我认为发言者提出了明确的请求。
p149.en: 6. If you choose this sentence, we are not in agreement. For me, “do not hide” is a vague request. If the speaker says, “Tell me, how do you see my performance in the meeting yesterday and give me some advice”, then I think the speaker has made a clear request.

p150.original: 7.如果你选择这一句，我们意见一致。
p150.en: If you choose this sentence, we agree.

p151.original: 8.如果你选择这一句，我们意见不一致。如果发言者说“我想多一些时间和你聊聊，不知道你是否愿意每周和我吃一次午饭”，那么，我认为发言者提出了明确的请求。
p151.en: 8. If you choose this sentence, we are not in agreement. If the speaker says, “I want to talk to you some more, and I wonder if you would like to have lunch with me once a week”, then I think he has made a clear request.

p152.original: 9.如果你选择这一句，我们意见不一致。对我来说，“尊重我的个人隐私”这个短语并不能清楚地表达发言者的请求。如果发言者说“在进我的办公室前，请先敲门好吗”，那么，我认为发言者提出了明确的请求。
p152.en: If you choose this sentence, we are not in agreement. For me, the phrase “respect my privacy” does not clearly convey the speaker's request. If the speaker says, “Can you knock before you enter my office”, then I think the speaker has made a clear request.

p153.original: 10.如果你选择这一句，我们意见不一致。对我来说，“经常”这个词并不能清楚地表达发言者的请求。如果发言者说“我希望你每周一晚上都可以做晚饭”，那么，我认为发言者提出了明确的请求。
p153.en: If you choose this sentence, we are not in agreement. For me, the word “often” does not clearly convey the request of the speaker. If the speaker says, “I hope you can cook dinner one night a week”, then I think the speaker has made a clear request.
